item.title: Google adds collapsible AI chat sidebar to homepage
item.description:
Google adds collapsible AI chat sidebar to homepage

Google is updating its homepage to include AI searches by adding a collapsible sidebar that allows users to view and continue their AI chats. This change introduces a new way to access recent AI Mode activities directly from the Google homepage, moving beyond the traditional single search bar.

🔍 Overview

The update integrates AI chat functionality directly into the Google homepage experience. Previously, users accessed AI features through the AI Mode button in the search bar, which opened a chatbot-like search experience. The new interface adds a persistent sidebar to manage these interactions.

🧩 How it works

Users can open the sidebar by clicking a gray bar that appears on the left side of the screen. From there, the interface displays a list of recent searches made using AI Mode. The sidebar provides tools to manage these conversations and initiate new interactions.

⚙️ Key details

The new sidebar includes the following features:

  • View a list of recent searches made using AI Mode
  • Start a new thread
  • Search existing threads
  • Connect a Gemini Notebook

This update follows other recent changes to Google’s search box, which in May was updated to accommodate longer queries and include AI-powered autocomplete. Last year, Google brought its AI Mode button to the search bar.

🚀 Availability

The new homepage layout is rolling out globally on desktop.

💡 Why it matters

Robby Stein, Google’s vice president of product, stated that the option is being rolled out because “people are coming to Search with more questions that aren’t just one and done.” Stein added that “in testing, this sidebar made a big difference for making progress & continuing to explore the web.”

#Google #AI #Search #ProductUpdates

Source: Google is putting AI chats right on the homepage

item.title: ChromaLeon: Dynamic GNOME Theme Accent Colors
item.description:
ChromaLeon: Dynamic GNOME Theme Accent Colors

ChromaLeon is a GNOME extension that dynamically changes accent colors based on your wallpaper. It’s a project maintained in spare time, with support for native GNOME accent colors and seamless application across GNOME Shell and GTK apps.

🔍 Overview

  • Change your GNOME Shell and GTK accent colors dynamically based on your wallpaper.
  • Change your GNOME Shell, Adwaita, adw-gtk3, and app/folder icons accent colors dynamically based on your wallpaper.
  • ChromaLeon was created within the context of the Adwaita theme.

🧩 How it works

  • Dynamic Extraction: Automatically extracts accent colors from your current wallpaper.
  • Applies accent colors seamlessly across GNOME Shell and GTK 3.0 / 4.0 apps.
  • Theme the Shell and all your LibAdwaita and GTK3 applications with Adw-GTK3.
  • Applies the accent color to the folders.
  • Applies the accent color to some app icons.
  • Includes a wallpaper selector for user wallpapers and GNOME dynamic wallpapers.
  • Allow applying custom CSS to the shell, with support for ChromaLeon’s accent color.
  • Hot Reload for GTK4 applications with support for ChromaLeon colors (works natively for GNOME colors).
  • Syncs color variables so your sandboxed Flatpak applications match the rest of the system.

⚙️ Key details

  • ChromaLeon conflicts DIRECTLY with the User Theme extension. If you have this extension installed, please REMOVE or DISABLE it to avoid any errors.
  • If you are experiencing any issues customizing applications or GNOME Shell, please ensure you are using the Adwaita theme before opening an issue.
  • A special thanks to PakoVM for the inspiration behind the tinted style. The implementation in ChromaLeon was based on an idea from his Tint My GNOME extension.

💡 Why it matters

  • ChromaLeon is a project I maintain in my spare time. If possible, please consider making a small donation to support my work!
  • Create a shortcut in the app grid to use this extension as an app.

🚀 Availability

  • ChromaLeon is available as a GNOME extension.

#GNOME #ChromaLeon #DynamicTheme #GTK #Adwaita

Source: Fabito02/ChromaLeon

item.title: AgnostUI Local v2 copies UI components into your project for AI readability
item.description:
AgnostUI Local v2 copies UI components into your project for AI readability

AgnostUI Local (v2) is a new CLI-based UI component library that copies components directly into your project at install time. Instead of keeping components hidden inside node_modules, the source code lands directly in your repository, providing full control and native integration with your framework.

🧩 How it works

AgnostUI components are authored as Lit Web Components, a standards-based layer over native Custom Elements. The CLI wraps these components for your specific framework at copy time. By default, components are placed under src/components/ag/, creating a dedicated namespace that keeps AgnosticUI components separate from your own code. This approach ensures that your design system does not fork when your tech stack changes.

🤖 AI and Agent Integration

Because the component source lives locally, it is readable by AI tools such as Cursor, Claude, Copilot, Windsurf, Aider, Gemini, Replit, Kiro, and Antigravity. Every tool sees the raw source, creating a high-fidelity environment for Generative UI and agent-driven interfaces.

  • Reduce Hallucination: Since the LLM reads local files like any other code, it knows exactly what is possible, preventing invented props or APIs.
  • Better Token Efficiency: Using semantic HTML and standard CSS provides clean context, allowing agents to spend fewer tokens to understand the UI for faster, more accurate generations.
  • Agent Skills: AgnosticUI Playbooks act as pre-defined skills, prompting agents to scaffold complex, accessible workflows using local components.

📜 Playbooks and Components

The schema-driven layer ships with three companion documents. AgnosticUI offers Playbooks that demonstrate modular, prompt-driven UI components. These Playbooks support agent-generated UI workflows directly.

Playbook Name Description
Login Form Demonstrates modular, prompt-driven UI components
Onboarding Wizard Demonstrates modular, prompt-driven UI components
Discovery Dashboard Demonstrates modular, prompt-driven UI components
Support Center Demonstrates modular, prompt-driven UI components
Data Grid Demonstrates modular, prompt-driven UI components
Blog / Article Reader Demonstrates modular, prompt-driven UI components
Landing / Marketing Page Demonstrates modular, prompt-driven UI components

💡 Why it matters

AgnostUI Local solves the “Black Box” problem of traditional libraries hidden in node_modules. It is designed as the architecture for the next era of development, characterized as context-aware, framework-agnostic, and AI-ready.

#AIagents #UILibraries #WebDevelopment #LitWebComponents #CodeGen #DesignSystems
